# One-sample t-test power calculation
# Parameters
n <- 25                    # sample size (participants)
alpha <- 0.05              # significance level
effect_size <- 0.2         # mean difference to detect
sd <- 0.5                  # standard deviation
null_mean <- 0             # null hypothesis mean

# Calculate non-centrality parameter
# ncp = sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)
ncp <- sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)

# For a one-sided test, we compute:
# Power = P(t_{n-1} > t_{critical} | ncp)
# where t_critical is the critical value at alpha level with df = n-1

df <- n - 1                # degrees of freedom

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is the probability of exceeding the critical value under the alternative
power <- 1 - pt(t_critical, df, ncp = ncp)

# Display results
cat("One-Sample t-Test Power Calculation\n")
cat("====================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size (n):           %d participants\n", n))
cat(sprintf("Null hypothesis:           μ = %.1f\n", null_mean))

# Step 2: Compute non-centrality parameter (ncp)
# Under H1, the t-statistic is distributed as t(df, ncp) where ncp = sqrt(n) * d

ncp <- sqrt(n) * cohens_d
cat("\nStep 2: Non-centrality Parameter\n")
cat(sprintf("df = n - 1 = %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("ncp = sqrt(n) × Cohen's d = sqrt(%d) × %.4f = %.4f\n", n, cohens_d, ncp))

# Step 3: Find critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
# For one-sided test with H1: μ > 0, we use the right tail
# t_crit = t_{1-α, df} = t_{0.95, 24}

cat("\nStep 3: Critical Value (One-Sided)\n")
cat(sprintf("For α = %.2f (one-sided), critical t = t_{%.2f, %d} = %.6f\n", 
            alpha, 1-alpha, df, t_crit))

# Power = P(T > t_crit | T ~ t(df, ncp))

null_mean <- 0             # null hypothesis mean

# Calculate non-centrality parameter
# ncp = sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)
ncp <- sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)

# For a one-sided test, we compute:
# Power = P(t_{n-1} > t_{critical} | ncp)
# where t_critical is the critical value at alpha level with df = n-1

df <- n - 1                # degrees of freedom

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is the probability of exceeding the critical value under the alternative
power <- 1 - pt(t_critical, df, ncp = ncp)

# Display results

cat("====================================\n")

null_mean <- 0             # null hypothesis mean

# Calculate non-centrality parameter
# ncp = sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)
ncp <- sqrt(n) * (effect_size / sd)

# For a one-sided test, we compute:
# Power = P(t_{n-1} > t_{critical} | ncp)
# where t_critical is the critical value at alpha level with df = n-1

df <- n - 1                # degrees of freedom

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is the probability of exceeding the critical value under the alternative
power <- 1 - pt(t_critical, df, ncp = ncp)
